exposure: Mode of IUD insertion during cesarean section (conventional manual vs. intra-cesarean post placental introducer withdrawal technique)
cohort: 840 women undergoing cesarean section who desired IUD insertion
finding: The new intra-cesarean post placental introducer withdrawal technique for IUD insertion during cesarean section was associated with lower rates of IUD displacement, non-visibility of threads, and higher continuation rates compared to the conventional manual technique.
mod_finding: The new intra-cesarean post placental introducer withdrawal technique for IUD insertion during cesarean section was associated with lower rates of IUD displacement, non-visibility of threads, and higher continuation rates compared to the conventional manual technique.
